messages:
Maya: Heads-up — saw a flurry of GPU node drains in eu-west-1 last night, lots of 1-GPU node churn. Apps saw increased OOMs and scheduling latency. Anyone digging into CA flags or pool configs? :thinking_face:
Sanjay: I noticed that too. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-down + immediate scale-up for small jobs. Likely due to small binpackable pods bouncing between pools.
Dana: Can you paste the CA decision logs? I want to see the reasons for eviction.
Maya: Pasted a short excerpt from the CA logs: ```ScaleDown: node gpu-small-5 evicted 3 pods - unneeded for 300s - utilization 0.12 - expected 0.08 -> scaleDown```. Seems like our unneeded time is low.
Leo: Current helm values for CA in prod: ```--scale-down-unneeded-time=3m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 --expander=least-waste --max-empty-bulk-delete=10``` That utilization threshold is pretty aggressive for mixed GPU workloads.
Sanjay: For GPUs we usually run --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m and --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.35 in dedicated pools. But small CPU-only pods co-located with GPU pods are confusing the packing heuristic.
Dana: Two quick ideas: 1) increase unneeded-time for GPU nodepools to 15m, 2) set expander to `priority` with weights that prefer GPU-dense nodepools, and 3) add safety for nodes with GPU-allocated volumes.
Maya: Agree. Also thinking about a capacity smoothing window to avoid oscillation when bursty jobs arrive. CA doesn't have built-in hysteresis for short bursts. Could we add a pre-filter: if recent scale-ups in last X minutes, inhibit scale-down?
Leo: We can mimic smoothing with `--scale-down-unneeded-time` + `--new-pod-scale-up-delay` (the latter prevents immediate downs after up). Example: set `--new-pod-scale-up-delay=5m` for GPU pools.
Sanjay: Another lever: taints/tolerations. If we taint gpu-small pools with `gpu-preemptible=true:NoSchedule` and only allow batch jobs, then interactive/latency-sensitive pods won't move and cause churn. But that requires pod selector changes.
Maya: Good point. We could also tweak the expander weight file. Proposed policy snippet: ```expander: priority weights: - name: gpu-dense weight: 100 - name: gpu-small weight: 30 - name: cpu-large weight: 10``` This biases scale-ups to gpu-dense pools.
Dana: Don't forget scale-down policies: `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false` (we want to consider system pods) and `--max-graceful-termination-sec=600` to give kubelet drain a longer window for GPUs.
Sanjay: Cost side: gpu-small are cheaper spot-backed instances; the churn is partially from preemptions. We should pass `--cloud-provider-filter` to prefer stable instance types for primary pools. Also consider `--scale-down-unready-time` to avoid removing nodes that are transiently unready after preemption.
autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler[prod/eu-west-1]: scaled up pool gpu-dense (3 -> 5) at 2025-09-10T23:04:12Z
Leo: Proposed rollout plan: 1) Stage in staging: set `--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m` and `--new-pod-scale-up-delay=5m` for gpu pools. 2) Add expander priority weights. 3) Monitor for 48h, check `scaleDown`/`scaleUp` counts. 4) If still noisy, add taint-based segregation for batch jobs.
Maya: I'll open the PR with the helm changes and a quick runbook. PR will include metrics to watch (node churn, pending pods, scheduling latency, pod evictions).
Dana: Also add a small e2e test that simulates bursty job arrival and validates no >2 churn events in 30m window.
Sanjay: SGTM. If we see persistent oscillation after those changes we can experiment with `--expander=most-pods` + binpack tweaks.
Maya: Thanks all — assigning followups: Maya to PR, Dana to e2e, Leo to update expander weights, Sanjay to audit instance type stability. Will report back in this thread. :thumbsup:
